slides.title: When Robots Rate Their Own Interactions: Engagement Validity and the Strangeness Failure
slides.highlight: This research explores inverted evaluation where LLM-powered robots rate their own interactions, providing insights into the boundary conditions of using AI for HRI assessment relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: LLM-powered robots can accurately rate user engagement but systematically fail to detect human feelings of strangeness.
card.key_idea: An 'inverted evaluation' framework where LLMs complete standardized HRI questionnaires from the robot's perspective using interaction transcripts and multimodal context to align with human ground truth.
card.evaluation: Tested via HRI-CUES dataset (1,522 evaluations across 5 LLMs) and a live Nao robot pilot (N=4) using Pearson r and ICC.
card.limitation: LLMs lack access to internal affective states, conflating philosophical engagement with comfort and failing to detect unexpressed strangeness.

slides.title: A Taxonomy of Conceptual Alignment in Human-Robot Dialogue
slides.tldr: TAXONOMY FOR CONCEPTUAL ALIGNMENT IN HRI
slides.highlight: This paper proposes a taxonomy and dialogue act schema for conceptual alignment in human-robot interaction, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: A design-centric taxonomy for analyzing and structuring conceptual alignment in human-robot dialogue.
card.key_idea: A framework characterizing alignment by initiation triggers (terminology, behavior, situation), five levels of conceptual representation, and a detailed dialogue act schema for interactional moves.
card.evaluation: Developed via literature review and empirical analysis of 48 human-human dialogues in a collaborative image-sorting task to capture natural alignment behaviors.
card.limitation: Based on controlled tasks and human-human data, potentially omitting in-the-wild dynamics and robot-specific constraints like perception or embodiment.

slides.title: Predictive Gaze Is Preserved but Reorganized toward Monitoring during Robot-Mediated Manipulation
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that predictive gaze is preserved during robot-mediated manipulation but shifts toward monitoring the end-effector, providing a signal for inferring action intentions relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: Predictive gaze is preserved but shifts toward monitoring during robot-mediated telemanipulation.
card.key_idea: Investigation of gaze behavior during goal-directed telemanipulation to determine how visuomotor control adapts to altered embodiment and disrupted sensorimotor coupling.

slides.title: SignVLA: Real-Time Sign Language-Guided Robotic Manipulation via Attention LSTM and Vision-Language-Action Models
slides.highlight: SignVLA introduces a framework that converts sign language gestures into semantic instructions for VLA policies, enhancing accessibility for deaf and speech-impaired users. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: SignVLA enables real-time robotic manipulation guided by sign language via a lightweight sign-to-text interface.
card.key_idea: MediaPipe landmarks are processed by an attention-enhanced LSTM and temporal buffer to generate natural-language instructions for a downstream GR00T VLA policy.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on ASL Citizen (recognition) and LIBERO (manipulation); achieved 88.89% top-1 accuracy and up to 98.5% task success rates.
card.limitation: Currently limited to isolated sign classification and simulation; real-world deployment and continuous sign understanding remain future work.

slides.title: Gold Points Sniper: Self-guided Visual Reasoning in VLM for Fine-grained Action Understanding
slides.tldr: SELF-GUIDED VISUAL REASONING FOR FINE-GRAINED ACTION UNDERSTANDING
slides.highlight: This framework enables lightweight VLMs to interpret fine-grained human actions and intentions, providing a foundation for safer human-robot interaction in domestic settings, which is relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: GPS enhances lightweight VLMs for fine-grained human action understanding using self-guided multimodal reasoning.
card.key_idea: A framework featuring a Gold Points Extractor for detail identification, a Selective Socratic Questioner for refinement, and a Semantic Entailment Evaluator for factual consistency assessment.
card.evaluation: Tested on a CAP-based dataset using lightweight VLMs (e.g., LLaVA-OV-7B) and GPT-4o; measured via a custom Semantic Entailment Score.
card.limitation: Complex multi-stage prompts can be cognitive burdens for lightweight VLMs without specific fine-tuning.

slides.title: Counterfactual learning of new adaptive instructional policies using logged data
slides.tldr: OFFLINE CONTEXTUAL BANDIT FRAMEWORK FOR ADAPTIVE TUTORING
slides.highlight: This work proposes an offline contextual bandit framework to optimize instructional policies using logged data, which is relevant to MIMIC's focus on LLM-based agent models and societal-scale simulation of human-AI interactions.

card.one_liner: An offline contextual bandit framework that learns adaptive instructional policies from logged ITS interaction data.
card.key_idea: Uses a Rasch model for latent proficiency-difficulty mapping and a reward function optimizing 'flow' to treat tutoring as a continuous stochastic bandit problem.
card.evaluation: Tested on four large-scale real-world datasets; results show consistent policy improvements over the logged behavior policy.

slides.title: Reference-Driven Multi-Speaker Audio Scene Generation from In-the-Wild Priors
slides.highlight: ScenA generates multi-speaker audio scenes with overlapping dialogue and ambient noise using reference voices and text prompts, contributing to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception of hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: ScenA generates multi-speaker audio scenes from natural language prompts and reference voices without structured supervision.
card.key_idea: A flow-matching model using latent concatenation and identity-aware positional encodings, employing a high-noise-biased timestep distribution to prevent the 'Reference Shortcut' where models ignore text prompts.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on CoVoMix2-Dialogue benchmarks using cpWER, cpSIM, and ACC; outperformed baselines in speaker-binding and human preference tests.
card.limitation: Limited to 20-second audio durations and a maximum of three reference speakers.
